About the Team

Engineering Tomorrow's Waters

A Fresh Start With a Proud History

The HSRW Submarine Team is a student-run engineering group at Hochschule Rhein-Waal, building a human-powered submarine from the ground up. The project goes back to 2007, with boats that have raced and won prizes across Europe and the USA. Now a new generation of students is rebuilding the team and the submarine, carrying the ambition forward with fresh energy, updated engineering, and a renewed drive to compete.

We bring together mechatronics, hydrodynamics, and hands-on fabrication — learning by building something that actually has to work underwater.

Discover the Team
Our Core Focus

What We're Building

Every part of the submarine is a chance to learn — from hull design to human-powered propulsion.

01

Human Powered

Driven entirely by pedal power. Designed for efficiency, endurance and control underwater.

02

Hull & Hydrodynamics

Shaping a low-drag hull that balances speed, stability and manufacturability.

03

Mechatronic Systems

Controls, sensors and drivetrain integration built and tested by the team.

Our Story

Nineteen Years Underwater

The boats have changed and so have the teams. The goal hasn’t: build a human-powered submarine and race it. Here is the path so far, and where we stand now.

Origins
2007

Sea Bomb

Built by Prof. Megill at the University of Bath, where he worked before joining HSRW. The boat that started the story, and an early sign of our biomimetic roots.

🏆 2nd Prize, Biomimetic2.09 knotsSea Bomb / Rivershark
2013

Sea Bomb becomes Rivershark

Renamed Rivershark and taken to the 12th International Submarine Races at NSWC Carderock in the USA. The team’s race diary tells the whole story: a broken window, a snapped crankshaft pin, and a first run where the nose pitched up and the boat shot to the surface like a cork.

Sea Bomb / RiversharkRead the race diary
The Innovation Years
2014

INIA

A new fish-inspired design: a tuna-shaped body driven by biomimetic fins instead of a propeller. It won the Outstanding Innovation Prize at the European Submarine Race in the UK.

🏆 Outstanding Innovation PrizeINIAWatch INIA in action
2015

INIA takes second place in Washington

Improved after the first race and taken to the 13th International Submarine Races near Washington D.C. Second place out of 24 teams from eight countries, plus first in Non-Propeller Female with pilot Leandra. On the last day the team swapped to river-dolphin fins, and it paid off.

🏆 2nd place overall🏆 1st Non-Propeller FemaleINIARead the press release
2016

Trichitala

Our most unusual design ever, and it won the Most Unusual Design prize. A big calculation error meant it never got to drive at the races, and the lesson stuck.

🏆 Most Unusual DesignTrichitalaWatch the first pool session
2017

Rivershark returns

Back at the 14th International Submarine Races with a new iteration of Rivershark, now with a Mirage drive system.

Sea Bomb / Rivershark
2018

Rivershark hits 2.89 knots

Frauke piloted Rivershark to victory in the Best Female Pilot category, and the sub took Best Biomimetic.

🏆 Best Biomimetic🏆 Best Female Pilot2.89 knotsSea Bomb / Rivershark
2019

Back in the pool

Rivershark in the water with the dive team.

Sea Bomb / Rivershark
The Pause
2020–21

Racing on hold

The pandemic stopped the races, and the team went quiet.

The Comeback
2022

Overall winner

Rivershark takes the Overall Winner title and Best Female Pilot at the European International Submarine Races. Our biggest result so far.

🏆 Overall Winner🏆 Best Female PilotSea Bomb / Rivershark
2023

Chelonia

A brand new submarine, built by Lysander and Joshua.

Chelonia
2024

Chelonia in Gran Canaria

Chelonia’s second season, this time in Gran Canaria.

Chelonia
2025

Rhine Ray

Rhine Ray didn’t make it. A tough year, and the lessons come with us into what is next.

Rhine Ray
Now
2026

We are rebuilding

A new team of ten is restarting the project: a new hull in development, a new emblem, and one clear goal. Get back in the water and race again.
